parties:
Anwar Hossain (Md) & another ------ Petitioners 
Vs 
Uttara Valley Ltd and other ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 2. The petitioners are amongst the subscriber share-holders of the Company. On incorporation of the Company the subscriber share-holders, six (6) in number subscribed 300 shares, of which the petitioner No. 1 subscribed 54 shares and petitioner No. 2 subscribed 48 shares and thus the petitioners acquired more than 30% of the subscribed shares in the Company. The petitioner No.1 was appointed as the first Managing Director of the company. The Company was incorporated on 28-11-94. The tenure of the petitioner as Managing Director, as per Articles of Association of the Company was for 3 years and subsequently the period was extended. The respondent-company purchased 25-08 acres of land vide registered sale deed and its name was duly mutated in the records of right in respect of 23.38 acres, as at the time of mutation 1.7 acres of land, out of the purchased 25.08 acres of land, was found to have been recorded as khas land. The petitioners were ousted from the management of the Company by the respondent Nos. 2-5, who conspired to grab the company's property. On 8-12-2002 petitioners received notice from the Upazila Land Office, Sylhet Sadar, (respondent No. 9) in connection with a mutation case in respect of the company's landed property and on query it was revealed that beyond the knowledge of the petitioners the respondent No. 3, who has been appointed as the Executive Director, sold company's landed property to the respondent Nos. 6-8 through six separate registered sale deeds and the said respondent Nos. 6-8 filed the mutation case in the office of the respondent No. 9 and on 12-12-02 the petitioner No. 1 filed objection there-against the office of the respondent No. 9 and accordingly, the proceeding was stayed. It was revealed from the copy of the sale deeds, procured subsequently, that the respondent No.3 without any authority from the Board of Directors of the Company illegally claiming his authority under Article 82 of the Articles of Association sold the company's land in reference and executed and registered the sale deeds for and on behalf of the Company in favour of the respondents Nos. 6-8 and that 22 acres of land were sold for Taka 6,70,000 and that the sale proceeds have not been deposited in the company's account. One of the purchasers is the respondent No. 7, who is the son of respondent No. 2; and another purchaser is respondent No. 8 who is the wife of the respondent No. 3, the executant of the sale deeds; and the other purchaser is respondent No. 6, who is a nephew of the respondent No. 2. The respondent Nos. 2-8 misappropriated the company's property in the aforesaid manner and that the affairs of the Company are being carried on to the prejudice and disregard of the interest of the petitioners and that petitioners could not move the Board of Directors or any General Meeting for taking any resolution against the fraudulent transaction of the respondents and that affairs of the Company were being managed by the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to the exclusion of the petitioner No. 1, though he is the Managing Director, and that the tenure of the petitioner as Managing Director has been extended for 5 years with effect from 20-11-02. The respondent No.3 is a practicing Advocate of Sylhet Judges Court and he drafted and prepared the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company and included Article 82 providing all powers of the Managing Director to the Executive Director and the respondent No. 3 is the named Executive Director in the Articles of Association for a period of 3 years and his tenure has not been extended further. The respondent No.3 bears bad reputation, he is involved in two (2) criminal cases, and that there was no resolution of the Board of Directors, as required under Article 82 (Kha) of the Articles of Association, authorising the respondent No. 3, as Executive Director, to exercise the authority given under Article 82 of the Articles of Association of the Company to execute and register any deed of sale for and on behalf of the company and that the Company never required or intended to sell the land in question and the land in question is alleged to have been sold by the Executive Director, (respondent No. 3) illegally in collusion with the Chairman (respondent No. 2) to the respondent Nos. 6-8 showing a very low price only because respondent No. 6 is the nephew of the respondent No. 2, (Chairman of the Company and respondent No. 7 is the son of the respondent No.2 and respondent No. 8 is the wife of the respondent No. 3(the executant) and that the sale of the land in question through respondent No. 3 in favour of the respondent Nos. 6-8 being without the required resolution of the Board of Directors, the whole transaction as to said sales is illegal and hence no legal right, title and interest has accrued in favour of the respondent Nos. 6-8 on the land in question and in order to stop delivery of possession of the land in question, the petitioner No. 1 made a General Diary at the Kotwali PS Sylhet, on 10-12-02 and that the purchasers being close relations of the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 there is no reason to believe that they had no knowledge about the internal disputes amongst the Directors of the Company and that for protection of the minority share-holders interest this Company can pass such orders as it deems fit including cancellation of any sale deed fraudulently made by any Director of the Company without obtaining authority from the Company and that the petitioner No. 1 did not write any letter to the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms, alleged to have been received on 18-12-02, for supply of certified copy of documents and did not submit any resolution book of the Board of Directors and of the General Meeting of the Company, and that in the record of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sylhet Sadar, relating to the mutation case for recording names, the respondent Nos. 6-8 against the land in reference, there is a noting to the effect that papers showing that Managing Director has handed over the charge of his office to the Executive Director (respondent No. 3), and a copy of the resolution of the Board of Directors authorising the Executive Director to exercise the powers under Article 82 of the Articles of Association were submitted but those papers however are not available in the said case record; and that the respondent No. 3, being a family lawyer and a trusted friend of the petitioners and the respondent Directors of the Company, was in possession of the title deeds of the Company's properties and he exploited his fiducial position to misappropriate Company's property and that the petitioners do not possess the proceeding books of the Directors' meetings and of the share-holders' meetings and that the copy of the papers and document, which they have in their possession, have been annexed with the affidavit. The petitioners have no other papers and documents of the Company. The petitioners filed this application to safeguard their interest as well as Company's interest in the Company's landed properties covered by the sale-deeds, evidenced by the Annexures F to F-5 to the application.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman
